title: [RPG Design Guides] Dungeon Balance ① What Makes a Dungeon Fun?

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】ダンジョンバランス① 面白いダンジョンとは？
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Dungeon Balance ① What Makes a Dungeon Fun?

blocks.source: ダンジョンは戦闘と並んで、プレイ時間の多くを占めることになる。
blocks.translation: Along with battles, dungeons will account for a large portion of the playtime.

blocks.source: 一般的にダンジョンのないＲＰＧは珍しいけれど、そもそもダンジョンとは何のために設けられるのだろうか？
blocks.translation: While RPGs without dungeons are generally uncommon, what are dungeons actually intended for in the first place?

blocks.source: 苦労させることで、達成感を演出する。
blocks.translation: Create a sense of accomplishment by making players work for it.

blocks.source: 探索する楽しさを表現する。
blocks.translation: Express the fun of exploration.

blocks.source: シナリオを様々な面で補強する。
blocks.translation: Reinforce the scenario in various ways.

blocks.source: プレイ時間を増加させることで暇つぶしに貢献する。
blocks.translation: Help pass the time by increasing the playtime.

blocks.source: などなど、適当に挙げてみた。
blocks.translation: Those are a few ideas I came up with off the top of my head.

blocks.source: ファミコン時代など昔のＲＰＧの中には、まるでプレイヤーを苦労させること自体が目的かのようなダンジョンも存在したが、基本的にはプレイヤーを楽しませるためのものである。その点を考慮して作成しよう。
blocks.translation: Some older RPGs, such as those from the Famicom era, featured dungeons that seemed to have the very purpose of making the player struggle. Basically, however, dungeons are meant to entertain the player. Keep that in mind when creating them.

blocks.source: では、そのためにも第一にダンジョンの長さに焦点を当てたい。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, I would first like to focus on dungeon length.

blocks.source: ダンジョンの長さを設定するに当たっては、プレイヤーがどのようにダンジョンを進んでいくのかを考慮する必要がある。通常は（僕を含め）宝箱などを漁りながら寄り道しながら進む人の方が多いはずであり、目的地に向かって一直線に進んで行く人はまれなはず。
blocks.translation: When setting a dungeon's length, you need to consider how players will make their way through it. Normally, most people (myself included) will proceed while searching through treasure chests and taking detours, while few will head straight toward their destination.

blocks.source: ダンジョンの長さを決めるに当たって忘れてはならないのは、ダンジョンの重要度。
blocks.translation: When deciding on a dungeon's length, you must not forget its importance.

blocks.source: 次の町に行くために通過するだけの重要度が低いダンジョンに数時間もかかる（例：ＦＦ１２、ワイルドアームズ５）のは勘弁して欲しいと誰もが思うところだし、主人公と因縁のあるボス敵が待ち構えるダンジョンならば、長くて手強いほうがメリハリがつく。
blocks.translation: Everyone would understandably hate to spend several hours in a low-importance dungeon that they only pass through to reach the next town (e.g., Final Fantasy XII and Wild Arms 5). On the other hand, if a dungeon is home to a boss enemy with a grudge against the protagonist, making it long and challenging can provide a good sense of contrast.

blocks.source: もっとも、重要度が高いダンジョンでも、ボス戦やイベントに専念させたいから、ダンジョン自体は短めに設定するというのも悪くない判断かも。
blocks.translation: That said, even for a high-importance dungeon, it may not be a bad idea to make the dungeon itself short if you want players to focus on the boss battle and events.

blocks.source: 以上を考慮した上で、具体的にダンジョンの入口から、攻略までの所要時間を挙げると……
blocks.translation: Taking the above into consideration, if we give specific estimates for the time required to clear a dungeon from its entrance onward…

blocks.source: 重要度が低いダンジョンで数十分～１時間程度
blocks.translation: Around several dozen minutes to one hour for a low-importance dungeon

blocks.source: 重要度が高いダンジョンで３０分～数時間程度
blocks.translation: Around thirty minutes to several hours for a high-importance dungeon

blocks.source: 程度が目安だろうか。
blocks.translation: Those would probably be good guidelines.

blocks.source: また、ボス戦闘後には基本的にすぐ出られるようにしよう。ボス戦後の後戻りなど消化試合のようなものでつまらない。
blocks.translation: Also, players should generally be able to leave immediately after the boss battle. Backtracking after a boss fight is boring, like playing out a foregone conclusion.

blocks.source: 脱出手段としては……
blocks.translation: Possible means of escape include…

blocks.source: ＤＱのリレミトの様な脱出魔法や脱出アイテム。
blocks.translation: Escape spells or items, such as DQ's Evac.

blocks.source: ワープポイント（セーブポイントなどと統合するのも良し。）
blocks.translation: Warp points (These can also be integrated with save points, for example.)

blocks.source: イベント終了後、勝手に画面が暗転し、入口に戻る。
blocks.translation: After the event ends, the screen fades to black automatically and the player returns to the entrance.

blocks.source: などがある。作品の雰囲気にあった手段を用意しよう。
blocks.translation: These are some options. Prepare a method that suits the atmosphere of your game.

blocks.source: 上記で挙げた時間はあくまで目安であり、長いダンジョンをプレイヤーに飽きさせないためには、それだけの内容を盛り込む必要がある。
blocks.translation: The times listed above are merely guidelines. To keep players from getting bored in a long dungeon, you need to include enough content to justify its length.

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example…

blocks.source: 途中で出現する魔物を変化させる。
blocks.translation: Change the monsters that appear along the way.

blocks.source: 宝箱を配置する。
blocks.translation: Place treasure chests.

blocks.source: 会話やボス戦などのイベントを入れる。
blocks.translation: Include events such as conversations and boss battles.

blocks.source: 仕掛けを用意する。
blocks.translation: Prepare gimmicks.

blocks.source: 景色で魅せる。
blocks.translation: Captivate players with the scenery.

blocks.source: などである。
blocks.translation: Those are some examples.

blocks.source: 数時間の間、仕掛けもイベントもなく、景色に変化がなく、延々と同じ敵と戦わせられるだけのようなダンジョンは苦行にしかならないので注意しよう。
blocks.translation: Be careful: a dungeon where players spend several hours with no gimmicks or events, no changes in scenery, and nothing but endless battles against the same enemies will become nothing more than an ordeal.

blocks.source: 同様に、ダンジョンは「プレイ時間を増加させることで暇つぶしに貢献する。」と記述したけれど、この考え方は正直なところお勧めできない。
blocks.translation: Similarly, although I wrote that dungeons can “help pass the time by increasing the playtime,” I honestly cannot recommend this way of thinking.

blocks.source: 昔ならともかく、今の時代はインターネットなどによって、タダでもそこそこ面白い娯楽が豊富に存在する。それらに勝らなければ結局、暇つぶしにもならない。それでは本末転倒というもの。よって、無理な引き伸ばしによって質が落ちることは避けたい。
blocks.translation: That may have worked in the past, but nowadays the Internet provides an abundance of reasonably entertaining free amusements. If your game cannot outdo them, it will not even serve to pass the time. That would defeat the purpose. Therefore, I want to avoid lowering the quality through forced padding.

blocks.source: 当然ながら、質が高くて、かつプレイ時間も長い作品を作りたいならば、それだけの手間が必要であることを覚悟しよう。
blocks.translation: Naturally, if you want to create a game that is both high-quality and long, be prepared to put in the necessary effort.

blocks.source: 今回の講座では、主に一つのダンジョンについて説明したが、一作品内でのダンジョン構成もバリエーション豊かなものにしたい。
blocks.translation: In this guide, I mainly discussed individual dungeons, but I also want the dungeon design within a single game to offer plenty of variety.

blocks.source: 洞窟
blocks.translation: Caves

blocks.source: 森、竹林、ジャングル
blocks.translation: Forests, bamboo groves, jungles

blocks.source: 草原、湿原、雪原
blocks.translation: Grasslands, marshes, snowfields

blocks.source: 山、火山、雪山
blocks.translation: Mountains, volcanoes, snowy mountains

blocks.source: 城、塔、基地、神殿
blocks.translation: Castles, towers, bases, temples

blocks.source: 遺跡、墓地、廃墟
blocks.translation: Ruins, graveyards, abandoned ruins

blocks.source: 海賊船、幽霊船
blocks.translation: Pirate ships, ghost ships

blocks.source: 地底、海峡、海底
blocks.translation: Underground areas, straits, seabeds

blocks.source: 適当に分類してみたけれど、同じ『洞窟』でも『鍾乳洞』『溶岩の洞窟』『海辺の洞窟』というようにさらに詳細に分類できるので色々と考えてみて欲しい。もちろん、それぞれダンジョンの種類に合わせて仕掛けや出現する敵などにも工夫を凝らそう。
blocks.translation: I grouped them somewhat arbitrarily, but even “caves” can be further divided into types such as “limestone caves,” “lava caves,” and “seaside caves,” so I would like you to give it some thought. Of course, you should also put effort into designing the gimmicks and enemies that appear to suit each type of dungeon.

blocks.source: 長編ＲＰＧともなると、一作品でダンジョン数が２０～３０程度にも達することになる。バリエーション豊かなダンジョンを用意することで、プレイヤーを飽きさせないようにしたい。
blocks.translation: In a long RPG, the number of dungeons in a single game can reach around 20 to 30. I want to keep players from getting bored by preparing a wide variety of dungeons.
